description: A scenario that did not exist when the cloud ramp was built. It is adopted through declarations alone: a scenario dependency (ledger-service), a resource (ledger-store, amd64 artifact only), server-side credential descriptors, one public_via_edge listener, one private provider-callback listener, declared persistent data and a recovery contract. Its declaration tree under declarations/ is what the closure reads; no cloud source names this fixture.

ledger-service.reason: declared dependency of the primary scenario

ledger-store.reason: declared resource of the primary scenario and of ledger-service

oracle.description: The orders table holds exactly the seeded rows after deploy, update and restore; the three declared routes (public API, private provider callback, public download prefix) resolve to the same listener and upstream before and after an update; the webhook signing key never leaves the target.

ownership.cleanup_owner: scenario-to-cloud fixture lease (routed test storage + owned target)
ownership.neighbor_invariant: Unrelated operator data, processes, files and network rules remain unchanged after setup and cleanup (P02-A03).
ownership.write_scope_invariant: Every SQL and file write made while the fixture is leased belongs to its lease scope and its owned target (P02-A02).

lifecycle.note: Setup and teardown argv are returned by the fixture owner at lease time as typed {verb, argv[]} actions; the in-process journey in api/generality drives the ramp against a fake target. Never a shell string.
